ROW.COLUMN: (ML/CU) High Risk Transactions: Focal High Risk Entity

Financial institutions must apply enhanced scrutiny to transactions involving high-risk entities, as such activity that may subject the institution to a greater risk of money laundering or fraud. Any account, customer, correspondent bank, or external entity found on a watch list is considered to be a high-risk entity. This scenario monitors transactions to and from high-risk entities during a specified Lookback Period.

The main objective of this pattern is to find focal entities with list risk level greater or equal to the scenario risk threshold value and which total count and amount values of all kind of transactions are checked with scenario conditions of alert generation.
The exact transactional count and amount values for each type of transaction (wire, cash, MI, journal) per each focal entity are calculated in the respective sub-rule.
Final assessment is done in the check-point where count and amount values of all kinds of transaction are summarized.
The objective of main rule is to create dataset populated with focal entities with list risk value greater or equal to the scenario risk threshold value having at least one transaction (wire, cash, MI, journal) checked with scenario Orion library parameters conditions.
The objective of the firs sub-rule is to select all wire transactions of the focal entity. Total count and amount values are calculated and store in appropriate bind variable
The objective of the second sub-rule is to select all MI transactions of the focal entity. Total count and amount values are calculated and store in appropriate bind variable
The objective of the fourth sub-rule is to select all cash transactions of the focal entity. Total count and amount values are calculated and stored in the appropriate bind variable
The objective of the third sub-rule is to select all journal transactions of the focal entity. Total count and amount values are calculated and stored in the appropriate bind variable
The objective of the first check-point is to summarize count and amount values of all kind of transactions and weed out all focal entity that fail to check with alert generation parameter.
The objective of the fourth sub-rule is to get relevant records from all transactional datasets in order to extract augmented information for matched focal entity, which was not extracted in the Primary Rule dataset.
